title: A fleet needs a lifecycle
brief: Agents multiply faster than reviews. Decide how every agent is inventoried, identified, permissioned, reviewed and retired, and which control plane holds the list, while the runtimes, clouds and licences behind your agents are still open.

blocks.text: Five stages from first commit to retirement

steps.title: Inventory
steps.md: Register every agent with a sponsor, purpose, data and tool access, runtime and risk tier. If it is not listed, it is not governed.

steps.title: Identity
steps.md: Give each agent its own identity, not a shared account or a developer's credentials. Choose autonomous or on-behalf-of mode per agent.

steps.title: Permissions
steps.md: Grant least privilege through reviewed roles or access packages. Gate irreversible tools with approval.

steps.title: Review
steps.md: Sponsors review purpose and access on a schedule, and again after a material change to model, tools or data.

steps.title: Retirement
steps.md: Disable the identity, revoke credentials, delete memory and data under retention rules and close the registry entry.

blocks.title: Where the inventory lives
blocks.intro: Whatever you choose, the inventory must name an accountable sponsor for every agent.

options.name: Agent 365 registry
options.summary: Microsoft's control plane to observe, govern and secure agents, with the registry in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
pros: Native integration for Microsoft platforms, an SDK for framework-built agents and registry synchronization for connected platforms such as Vertex AI and AWS Bedrock
Entra, Purview and Defender in one plane
cons: Per-user licensing. Microsoft E5 is the best-fit prerequisite
Discovery of local and shadow agents through Defender and Intune was announced as preview on 2026-05-01
options.bestWhen: Most agents run on Microsoft platforms or can register, and you already run Entra, Purview and Defender.
options.avoidWhen: You have no Microsoft 365 footprint, or you operate in segments the Commercial GA announcement did not cover.

options.name: Entra Agent ID identities and sponsors only
options.summary: Use agent identities with sponsors as the spine and add controls as budget allows.
pros: Agent ID is available to Entra customers
Every agent gets an identity and a business sponsor
cons: Conditional Access and ID Governance for agents need a Microsoft 365 E7 or Agent 365 licence
No registry views or observability on their own
options.bestWhen: A small fleet, accountable identities needed first, licence budget still open.
options.avoidWhen: Agents live outside Entra, or you need a registry and observability.

options.name: Self-run registry with CI gates
options.summary: A catalogue you own, with pipeline checks that block unregistered deployments.
cons: You build discovery, reviews and retirement
options.bestWhen: A mixed or sovereign estate that Microsoft's plane does not reach.
options.avoidWhen: A small Microsoft estate where licensing is simple.

options.name: Per-team spreadsheets
options.summary: The boring option: each team keeps its own list.
options.bestWhen: A handful of agents in a pilot.
options.avoidWhen: Any agent that can send data out or change records.

items.symptom: A review finds live agents whose sponsor left the company.
items.cause: No succession process. Sponsors are required, but sponsorship has to be maintained when people move or leave.
items.fix: Use supported groups or two sponsors, alert on departures and make sponsor transfer part of offboarding.

items.symptom: An agent can read far more than its task needs.
items.cause: Permissions were copied from a developer or granted once and never reviewed.
items.fix: Use one identity per agent, least-privilege access packages and scheduled access reviews.

items.symptom: An agent nobody registered sends customer email.
items.cause: A shadow agent was built outside the registry, locally or as a SaaS agent.
items.fix: Add discovery (preview as of 2026-05-01 in Agent 365), registry synchronization, a CI gate for deployments and an egress review.

items.symptom: A retired agent's credentials still work.
items.cause: Retirement stopped at hiding the agent. Credentials, memory and data stayed.
items.fix: Disable the identity, revoke credentials on the blueprint, delete memory and data per retention and remove its tools.

items.symptom: Behaviour changed after a model upgrade, but the last review was a year ago.
items.cause: Reviews are tied to the calendar, not to change.
items.fix: Trigger a review on material change, and keep a periodic review as the floor.

items.title: Go deeper: Entra Agent ID objects and execution modes

blocks.md: A **blueprint** is a template that holds the credentials and permissions. An **agent identity** is a service principal with `servicePrincipalType` `ServiceIdentity` and has no credentials of its own: the blueprint uses its credentials to acquire tokens for the identities created from it. An optional **agent user** is a user object for the agent and needs the Frontier preview. Pick the execution mode first: **S2S** (the agent acts as itself with application permissions), **OBO** (the user is the token subject, the agent identity is the actor, delegated permissions) or **Agentic-User** (the agent acts as its own user account, Frontier preview) [[r27]].

The Agent 365 SDK adds identity, governed tooling and notifications. It does not build, host or run the agent, and the Agent 365 Observability SDK is deprecated in favour of the Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro.

blocks.title: What interviewers listen for
blocks.md: Name the five stages, then say who is accountable at each one: a sponsor for purpose and lifecycle, an owner for technical changes. Mention the OWASP agentic risks that bear on it, ASI03 Identity and Privilege Abuse and ASI09 Human-Agent Trust Exploitation [[r22]].

quiz.q: Put the agent governance lifecycle in order.
items: Inventory the agent with an accountable sponsor
Give it its own identity, not a shared account
Grant least-privilege permissions through reviewed access
Review purpose and access on a schedule and after change
Retire it: disable, revoke credentials and delete data
quiz.explain: You cannot give an identity to an agent you have not listed, you cannot scope permissions without an identity, and reviews only mean something once access exists. Retirement closes the loop by removing credentials and data so the agent cannot come back as a zombie.

quiz.q: A quarterly review finds agents that still run with live credentials after their business owner left. Which gap does this show?
options: Missing Conditional Access on the agent
No sponsor succession and review process
The agent used OBO instead of S2S
The registry showed duplicate rows for one agent
quiz.explain: Sponsors are required so every agent has an accountable business owner, but sponsorship must be maintained when a sponsor moves or leaves, and sponsors decide retention in access reviews. Conditional Access governs token issuance, the execution mode does not change who is accountable, and duplicate rows can be normal for a Copilot Studio agent.

quiz.q: Your estate has Foundry agents plus agents on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, and you want one inventory without rebuilding agents. What fits?
options: Agent 365 registry, with registry synchronization for the connected platforms
A Foundry project list, because Foundry hosts all agents
A shared spreadsheet maintained by each cloud team
Agent users in the Frontier preview for every agent
quiz.explain: Agent 365 describes three integration paths: native for Microsoft platforms, the SDK for framework-built agents and registry synchronization for connected platforms such as Vertex AI and AWS Bedrock. A Foundry list does not cover other clouds, a spreadsheet gives no discovery or enforcement and agent users are an identity feature, not an inventory.

takeaways: Five stages: inventory, identity, permissions, review, retirement. An unlisted agent is an ungoverned agent.
Every agent needs a sponsor for purpose and lifecycle. Plan for sponsor succession.
Agent 365 went GA on 2026-05-01 for the Commercial segment. Shadow-agent discovery was announced as preview.
Agents have no MFA. Govern them with Conditional Access and access packages, which carry licence requirements.
Retire completely: identity, credentials, memory, data and registry entry.
